minutes.headline: Board accepted the Assistant Town Manager/HR Director job description, one member opposed, and advanced a special event license policy.
minutes.summary: Public comment was dominated by Lake Shirley residents worried about weed and algae treatment and a dispute with the Conservation Commission; the chair said it would be taken up at a meeting the next day. The board then accepted the draft position description for the assistant town manager/HR director, held a policy workshop on a special event license policy, and trimmed bullet points for the town manager evaluation form. The town manager reported on grants, the MS4 permit, vacancies and road projects.

what_happened.line: The Select Board accepted the draft assistant town manager/HR director position description, with one member opposed, so the town manager can advertise the job.
The board held a workshop on a special event license policy and agreed draft changes, including a license rather than a permit, a 100-person trigger and 200-foot abutter notice.
The special event policy is set to return on August 6; the board also pared down the bullet points on the town manager evaluation form by consensus.
Lake Shirley residents used public comment to press the board on weed and algae treatment and an extension of the order of conditions needed to treat this summer.
The town manager reported on a state earmark, a recycling grant, MS4 engineering services and vacancies.

why_it_matters: The new assistant town manager/HR director position adds a salaried town staff post, paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, and the pay grade set now shapes that cost.
The special event rules would decide when organizers need a license and pay for advertising and abutter notice, which touches neighbors of events and anyone who holds one.
Whether Lake Shirley is treated this summer depends on an order of conditions extension, which bears on lake use and on association dues that fund treatment.
watch_next: August 6 Select Board meeting: the special event license policy returns, and a workshop on remaining policies is planned.
The extension of the Lake Shirley order of conditions, which the chair said would be taken up at a meeting the next day.
